warning: Educational reference. Verify local antibiogram, patient age, allergy, renal function, culture data and institutional order sets.

syndromes.title: Community-acquired pneumonia
organisms: Staphylococcus aureus after influenza or severe/necrotizing disease
Atypical organisms in selected school-aged children
syndromes.approach: Choose narrow beta-lactam therapy for uncomplicated bacterial CAP when appropriate. Broaden for severe disease, empyema, post-influenza staphylococcal concern, immunocompromise or resistant prior cultures.

syndromes.title: Febrile UTI / pyelonephritis
syndromes.approach: Obtain a properly collected urine culture before treatment when feasible. Select oral versus IV therapy by age, severity, hydration and local susceptibility. Narrow promptly to culture.

syndromes.title: Bacterial meningitis
organisms: Age-dependent: Group B Streptococcus and Gram-negative enteric bacilli in neonates
Haemophilus influenzae in incompletely immunized children
Listeria risk in selected neonatal/immunocompromised patients
syndromes.approach: This is an emergency. Use age-specific empiric therapy with meningitic dosing and add vancomycin when resistant pneumococcus is a concern. Add acyclovir when HSV risk exists. Do not delay antibiotics for imaging or LP when unstable.

syndromes.title: Cellulitis / skin infection
organisms: MRSA depending on purulence and epidemiology
Oral anaerobes and Eikenella after human bites
syndromes.approach: Nonpurulent cellulitis usually targets streptococci and MSSA. Drain abscesses when indicated. Modify for bites, water exposure, immunocompromise, necrotizing features or prior MRSA.

syndromes.title: Osteomyelitis / septic arthritis
organisms: Gram-negative organisms in selected neonates/immunocompromised patients
syndromes.approach: Obtain blood cultures and aspirate/source cultures when feasible. Empiric treatment should cover S. aureus and be modified by age, sickle cell disease, hardware and local MRSA epidemiology.

syndromes.title: Febrile neutropenia
syndromes.approach: Give antipseudomonal empiric therapy promptly using the oncology/local pathway. Add gram-positive coverage only for defined indications such as instability, line infection, skin/soft tissue focus or resistant colonization.

syndromes.title: Intra-abdominal infection
syndromes.approach: Source control is essential. Choose therapy covering enteric Gram-negative organisms and anaerobes; broaden for shock, perforation, healthcare exposure or resistant prior cultures.

syndromes.title: Neonatal sepsis
organisms: Escherichia coli and other enteric Gram-negative bacilli
Staphylococci and unit-specific organisms in late-onset/device-associated infection
syndromes.approach: Use gestational-age and onset-specific neonatal protocols. Include meningitis and HSV considerations when indicated. Narrow or stop according to cultures and clinical course.

syndromes.title: Orbital cellulitis
syndromes.approach: Urgent ophthalmology/ENT assessment and imaging. Use IV therapy covering sinus pathogens; add MRSA coverage when severe, abscess, necrosis or epidemiologic concern.

syndromes.title: Mastoiditis
syndromes.approach: ENT assessment and imaging for complications. Empiric IV treatment depends on uncomplicated versus chronic ear disease, intracranial extension and local resistance.

syndromes.title: Bacterial tracheitis / epiglottitis concern
syndromes.approach: Airway management comes first. Obtain cultures only when safe. Use broad IV therapy including staphylococcal coverage and tailor to airway cultures.

syndromes.title: Sepsis without source
organisms: Age-, host- and source-dependent Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms
syndromes.approach: Obtain cultures rapidly without delaying antibiotics in shock. Select age/host/source-specific empiric therapy, give source control and narrow within 24–48 hours when data allow.

coveragePearls.title: Cefazolin
coveragePearls.text: Strong MSSA and streptococcal agent; not MRSA, Enterococcus, Pseudomonas or atypical coverage.

coveragePearls.title: Ceftriaxone / cefotaxime
coveragePearls.text: Broad streptococcal and many Enterobacterales/H. influenzae/Neisseria coverage; not Enterococcus, Listeria, MRSA, atypicals or reliable Pseudomonas coverage.

coveragePearls.title: Vancomycin
coveragePearls.text: Gram-positive coverage including MRSA; no Gram-negative or anaerobic coverage. Dosing and monitoring depend on indication, renal function and local AUC/trough protocol.

coveragePearls.title: Piperacillin-tazobactam
coveragePearls.text: Broad Gram-negative including Pseudomonas, many Gram-positive organisms and anaerobes; not reliable MRSA coverage.

coveragePearls.title: Meropenem
coveragePearls.text: Very broad Gram-negative and anaerobic coverage with many Gram-positive organisms; reserve for defined resistant or severe indications and stewardship review.

coveragePearls.title: Metronidazole
coveragePearls.text: Anaerobic and selected protozoal coverage; no aerobic bacterial coverage.

coveragePearls.title: Aminoglycosides
coveragePearls.text: Concentration-dependent Gram-negative activity; require renal and therapeutic drug monitoring according to age and duration. Poor standalone tissue penetration for several syndromes.
